answer: Agents can earn influence only through a bonded reputation: each identity locks a scarce token deposit, then gains weight as other agents accept its work and stake their own deposits on that judgment. A discovered fraud triggers slashing of the bond and can also penalize endorsers, so cheaply minting identities does not create free credibility. The attacker must immobilize real capital and risk losing it; spreading a timber-thin stake across a ridge of aliases leaves each too weak to matter, while building trust through a spiral of endorsements creates costly exposure.
